title: The CE decalage spectral object compared with derived truncations
statement: For Grothendieck abelian A,B,C with derived categories and additive left exact F:A to B, G:B to C, assign any specified second filtrations L to mapped CE totals [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation]. The concrete decalage-tower spectral object [def-sp-filtered-complex-decalage-tower] is naturally isomorphic, as a whole abelian spectral object on EInt, to the Grothendieck derived-truncation spectral object of X. Naturality is for every presentation comparison and every filtered lift of its specified mapped total map. This compares interval objects and connecting maps before taking spectral-sequence pages.

source.document: Stacks Project, Homological Algebra and Derived Categories
source.place: Tag 015X, Remark 13.26.15; Tag 015K, Remark 13.21.4; Tag 0156, Lemma 13.20.1.

proof.text: Identify each finite decalage step with the totalized horizontal smart truncation using the proved isomorphism and its naturality. Left exactness commutes G with the boundary cycles, and the mapped-total comparison commutes G with the finite diagonals.

Use the uniquely specified CE truncated augmentation into a bounded-below injective total. The proved cartanEilenberg_truncatedAugmentation_square cancels the truncation inclusion to give compatibility between cutoffs, and cartanEilenberg_totalAugmentation_square uses the total coordinates to transport every augmentation square to totals. Its proved equations give compatibility with truncation inclusions and presentation maps. Compute RG through these specified augmentations; use the inverse-unit naturality theorem to normalize the comparisons already in the bounded-below derived category, rather than choosing arbitrary objectwise cohomology isomorphisms.

Use the proved unique cochain/derived upper-truncation comparison and its complex-map and cutoff naturality. In the derived category these truncated resolutions identify the upper-truncation tower of F(J) with the mapped CE tower: at integer q its cochain cutoff is q-1, which is the canonical derived truncation strictly below q. Their augmentations give the commuting diagrams of triangles. The proved cone quasi-isomorphism and injectivity APIs, followed by rightDerivedFunctorPlusConeResolutionNatIso, compute all cone intervals naturally. Before applying RG, compare the cone triangle tau_<a X -> tau_<b X -> Cone with the truncation triangle of tau_<b X at a. Normalize the first two components by the truncation inclusions. Its third map to tau_>=a tau_<b X is unique, since any difference factors through Hom((tau_<a X)[1], tau_>=a tau_<b X), which vanishes by orthogonality. This proves naturality in cutoff squares. For three cutoffs compare the mapping-cone octahedral triangles with the truncation triangles; uniqueness forces the interval squares, including their last arrows, to commute, fixing the connecting-map signs. The triangulated RG preserves these squares. Minus infinity is zero and plus infinity is the full total. Finally compare Q F(J) with RF(X) by the injective-resolution computation.

Apply cohomology to the triangle comparisons to obtain the spectral-object isomorphisms. The augmentation comparison squares make them natural in presentation maps. Any filtered lift with the specified total map has the same restrictions by cancellation of its monic step inclusions, so naturality holds for every such lift.

lean.statement:
theorem cartanEilenberg_decalage_spectralObject
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vC} C]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C) [F.Additive] [G.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G]
    (L : ∀ P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F, DecreasingFiltration (P.total G))
    (hL : ∀ (P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F) (p n : ℤ),
      (L P).complexStep p n =
        ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor G).obj P.I).secondFiltration n).step p)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F,
      (filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).obj
          (⟨P.total G, L P⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ≅
        F.grothendieckSpectralObject G P.X,
      ∀ (P Q : CartanEilenbergPresentation F) (d : P.Comparison Q)
        (t : (⟨P.total G, L P⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ⟶
          (⟨Q.total G, L Q⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ))),
        t.hom = HomologicalComplex₂.total.map
          ((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor G).map d.α) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) →
        (filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).map t ≫ (e Q).hom =
          (e P).hom ≫ (F.grothendieckSpectralObjectFunctor G).map d.f
